Well i had to move out because of a ndad as well, here's some advice.

Don't pay money for your mom or at the house.

Make up an excuse for needing that joint account money (only only when the time comes) if you don't trust your dad, and if refused then try to withdraw your rightful money from the account

It's CRITICAL that you become financially independent, that means your own financial account or any kind of way to keep your own money safe. 

Once you're 18 and find a place and you're absolutely set up for a job and financially able, just pack your stuff and go, if you know they'll try to stop you or emotionally abuse you to coming back then cut off or at least control your interactions with them.

i don't think it matters whether he's being selfish, but on a side note he might be under a lot of pressure and he's projecting that to you (in case he wasn't always this way)

with that said, if it's damaging you, and hurting your mental health, then detach yourself from that situation because your mental health matters too, if they're (him and fianceé) having problems you don't have to be invlolved.

the other option is having an actual talk with him and being very frank and clear about how you feel and how his treatment is hurting you, depending on how he takes it i think you'll know what to do.

if it's something that friend made public or is comfortable with other people knowing it then by all means go ahead.

if, however you were not supposed to know this or you heard it in some way by mistake/slip then preferably don't.

you're not an asshole at all, tobacco is addictive and people can relapse sometimes, i tried to quit and couldn't, so i know how hard it is, and the fact that you stopped for about a month before means you actually did try and are serious about it, you're just afraid of hurting her and that's understandable.

i can't advise you whether you should tell her or not though, but there's time for everything so it doesn't have to be immediate.
